paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: love isn't a feeling you wait on, it's something you DO. Paul says, "Love must be sincere," and then he spends the whole passage showing what that looks like (Romans 12:9). Share what you have, open your door, rejoice with the happy, weep with the hurting (Romans 12:13, 15). Sincere love has hands and feet, and it shows up even when the couch is calling its name.

Now the hard part, and I'm not going to dodge it. Paul says to bless those who persecute you, and not to repay evil for evil (Romans 12:14, 17). He says, "If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone" (Romans 12:18). Notice that he only asks you to do your part, and you can't control theirs. Then he says to leave room for God's wrath, because "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord" (Romans 12:19). Friend, that is a LOAD off your shoulders. You were never hired for that job, and the One who holds it is better at it than you are.

So here's what to carry out of my bakery today. Paul ends with "Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good" (Romans 12:21). When someone treats you badly, you get a choice: let it turn you into them, or answer with something better. Feed the hungry enemy, bless the one who cursed you, and keep your fire burning for the Lord (Romans 12:11, 20). That's how good wins, one small, stubborn act of love at a time.
